editorial.headline: The Quiet Work Behind Every Flight Approval
editorial.standfirst: A flight-approval agent handles the permissions, clearances and administrative representation that allow an operator’s planned flight to proceed.
editorial.body:
Flight approval is the unglamorous but consequential work that sits between an operator’s intended route and the authorities able to approve it. This activity covers intermediary services performed on an aviation operator’s behalf: arranging permission to cross airspace, securing landing permission, seeking airport time slots, and handling other operational clearances with the relevant civil or military aviation authorities. It also includes the related administrative and representative service. The activity is about obtaining approval, not operating an aircraft.

The record places this work within a digital-trade setting. It identifies electronic-trading-system providers and intermediary-platform providers that are not exempt, whether established inside Indonesia’s legal jurisdiction or established outside it while conducting electronic-trade business in Indonesia. The available business scales are broad: micro, small, medium and large. That matters because the code describes a specialised aviation-facing intermediary role without reserving it, in the record, for one particular business size.

Nationally, the position is clear. Foreign investment is permitted, and the foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%. In practical terms, the national record permits this activity to be wholly foreign-owned. Its stated basis is Presidential Regulation 10/2021 and 49/2021. That national openness should not be mistaken for a universal local registration outcome, however; the Bali treatment turns on the precise scope declared in the live OSS process.

Bali’s status is scope-dependent rather than categorically blocked. The province permanently blocks all low- and medium-low-risk KBLI activities for PMA registration across the island. For this activity, the record says that some scope may be low risk at large scale while other scope is assessed more highly. PMA registration in Bali is therefore available only where the business declares the higher-risk scope, with the record giving PPMSE in platform-trade cases as an example. The practical conclusion is narrow but important: a foreign investor cannot rely on the national 100% ceiling alone; the exact activity declared must support the higher-risk route in live OSS.
